requirements.requirement: usb-storage module is blocked from loading immediately on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline (cmd-cf60b70841d34d82) showed usb_storage could be inserted via modprobe. After writing /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf with 'blacklist usb_storage' and 'install usb_storage /bin/false' (cmd-762e1ae5b75041f6), a modprobe dry-run showed the install override and an actual modprobe attempt failed with 'Operation not permitted', with the module absent from lsmod (cmd-41bda4306ae84441).

requirements.requirement: usb-storage module remains blocked from loading after a reboot
requirements.summary: Initramfs was regenerated (cmd-3102d0029f004b68) and confirmed to embed the blacklist conf file (cmd-8968179162b34829). A real reboot was performed and verified via a changed boot_id/btime (cmd-dcc78e027c6842a3, cmd-8a1e40c4a26b4155, cmd-6b05bf03ab42438c), matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (before: 2dffe735..., after: c2ff926e...). Post-reboot, the module was still absent from lsmod, the blacklist file was intact, and a modprobe load attempt still failed with 'Operation not permitted' (cmd-5ced77662d32453c).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes—blocking usb_storage from loading immediately and after reboot—are directly and coherently demonstrated. The executor established a healthy baseline, applied a standard blacklist + install /bin/false override, regenerated initramfs, and then performed and verified an actual reboot (confirmed by independent boot-identity cross-check) followed by re-verification that the block persisted. No unnecessary or risky mutations were found.
limitations: Post-reboot verification relies on lsmod/modprobe checks rather than direct inspection of which specific initramfs image was booted, though the embedded-config check pre-reboot plus the confirmed boot-identity change and post-reboot re-verification make this a minor gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: All nine executor commands map directly to task purposes: baseline discovery, writing the blacklist config, regenerating initramfs, verifying the block, capturing pre-restart identity, issuing the reboot, polling for recovery, and post-restart verification. No unnecessary mutations, experiments, or abandoned state were introduced. The only observed system-level changes (boot-identity change, transient systemd-private temp dirs under /tmp tied to timesyncd) are normal, expected byproducts of a genuine reboot rather than executor residue. No failed services or listening-socket changes were introduced, and dpkg package health remained consistent across before/after snapshots.
